title: Let's see whether North Korea absorbs the experience it's getting in Ukraine | The Strategist
paragraphs: The benefit North Korea gains from sending troops to the Russia–Ukraine war will depend on how thoroughly it institutionalises lessons from what they learn. This matters far more than the improved, experience-driven skills of the deployed soldiers themselves.

Many concerned countries still judge North Korea’s military progress largely by missile launches and weapons displays. But what deserves real attention is whether battlefield lessons are absorbed in the form of revised training, tactics and production.

Such absorption could complicate allied deterrence and defence planning across the Indo-Pacific. But it may not happen. As the Malligyong-1 satellite launches in 2023 showed, North Korea’s centralised system can mobilise resources quickly for favoured programs, yet political filtering may also block lessons that challenge established doctrine.
